mainTopic: Who measures for the עגלה ערופה, and how many people value מעשר שני, הקדשות, and ערכין
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching that the measuring for the עגלה ערופה must be done even when the closest city is obvious. The גמרא notes that our משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who adds the מלך and the כהן גדול to the judges who go out. It then asks whether he also requires the entire סנהדרין. רב יוסף tries to prove that he does, from a ברייתא about a זקן ממרא who rebelled against the full court at בית פגי. אביי pushes back: perhaps the court went out to enlarge the city. A second ברייתא then names measuring for the עגלה outright, which supports רב יוסף. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's rule that three people value מעשר שני whose value is unknown: they must be experienced buyers, and even a גוי or the owner can be one of them. רבי ירמיה asks whether partners sharing one purse count as three, and the proof offered is pushed off. On הקדשות, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires ten, based on שמואל's count of 'כהן'. The גמרא cannot find a source for the רבנן's three and ends with 'קשיא'. Finally, רב גידל explains 'ערכין of movable property' as a vow to give the ערך of a utensil. A supporting teaching of his begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Measuring is required even when the closest city is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of a teaching: even if the body was found clearly next to a city, the judges must still carry out the measuring.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if the body was found obviously near a city, they must still do the measuring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching that started earlier. Even when it is obvious which city is closest to the dead body, the measuring for the עגלה ערופה must still be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Measuring is not just a way to find out which city is closest. It is part of the מצוה itself. So even when there is nothing to find out, the judges still have to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: Measuring the distance from the body to the nearby cities
The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown

phrases.english: [Even if it was found] clearly close to the city,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous amud about where the dead body was found.

phrases.english: they must involve themselves with the measuring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the teaching on measuring that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measuring for עגלה ערופה is required even when the closest city is obvious.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who adds the king and high priest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads 'your elders' as the סנהדרין and 'your judges' as the מלך and the כהן גדול, which is not how our משנה rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow this תנא. A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, 'And your elders and your judges shall go out.' 'Your elders' means the סנהדרין. 'Your judges' means the king and the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different opinion about who goes out to measure. According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the סנהדרין, the מלך, and the כהן גדול must all go out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה has only a small group of judges going out: three according to רבי שמעון, five according to רבי יהודה. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads the two words of the פסוק as two separate groups. 'Elders' are the סנהדרין, and 'judges' are the מלך and כהן גדול. That makes the group much bigger and more important than the משנה's.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה does not follow this תנא

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is not arguing about whether there is measuring. He agrees there is. He is arguing about WHO has to go out to do it.

phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with this tanna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
"And your elders and your judges shall go out,"
"Your elders": this is the Sanhedrin;
"and your judges": this is the king and the High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from how the measuring is done to who must take part in it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the סנהדרין, the מלך, and the כהן גדול go out for עגלה ערופה.

steps.title: פסוקים showing the king and high priest are called judges
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves that the מלך and the כהן גדול are each called a 'judge' in a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The king, as it is written: 'The king by justice establishes the land.' The כהן גדול, as it is written: 'And you shall come to the כהנים, the לוים, and to the judge.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא backs up its reading. It shows from פסוקים that the king and the כהן גדול count as 'judges.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: To read 'your judges' as the מלך and כהן גדול, the ברייתא must show that each of them is called a judge. The king is linked to justice in משלי. The 'judge' who sits next to the כהנים in דברים is taken to mean the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: The king, as it is written:
"The king by justice establishes the land."
The High Priest, as it is written:
"And you shall come to the priests the Levites, and to the judge."
phrases.notes: דברים יז:ט. The 'judge' mentioned next to the כהנים here is taken to be the כהן גדול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading in Step 2 with פסוקים.
steps.raayaObject: That the מלך and the כהן גדול count as 'judges'

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר בן יעקב argue on one point or two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי אליעזר בן יעקב only adds the מלך and כהן גדול, or also requires the entire סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Does רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagree on one point or on two? Does he disagree only about the king and the כהן גדול, while about the סנהדרין he follows either רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון? Or maybe he disagrees about the סנהדרין too, because he holds that we need the whole סנהדרין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about how far רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's argument goes. Does 'סנהדרין' mean a few judges, like in the משנה, or all of them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: he adds only the מלך and כהן גדול, and for the judges he agrees with רבי יהודה (five) or רבי שמעון (three). Option two: he also argues that the entire סנהדרין must go out. The question is what he means when he says 'סנהדרין.'

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
Does he disagree on one point or on two?

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב בַּחֲדָא פְּלִיג
phrases.english: Does Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov disagree on one matter
or does he disagree on two?
He disagrees about the king and the High Priest,
but regarding the Sanhedrin

phrases.aramaic: אִי כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אִי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: he holds either like Rabbi Yehuda or like Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: These are the two opinions in our משנה: רבי יהודה says five judges, רבי שמעון says three.

phrases.english: Or perhaps he disagrees about the Sanhedrin too,
in that he says: we need the entire Sanhedrin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the opinion quoted in Step 2 goes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires all the members of the סנהדרין, or only three or five judges plus the מלך and כהן גדול.

steps.title: רב יוסף begins a proof from the rebel elder at בית פגי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא about a זקן ממרא who rebelled against the סנהדרין at בית פגי. The rebellion does not count, because only 'the place' gives it legal force.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear. If he found them at בית פגי and rebelled against them, you might think his rebellion counts as a rebellion. So the פסוק says, 'And you shall arise and go up to the place.' This teaches that the place is what makes it count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף starts answering the question by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא describes the סנהדרין sitting outside its proper place, at בית פגי. The גמרא is setting up the proof here; it will spell out the inference next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא rules that rebelling against the סנהדרין at בית פגי is not a legal rebellion. The פסוק says 'go up to the place,' so the סנהדרין's authority depends on where it sits. What matters for our question is that the ברייתא imagines the סנהדרין at בית פגי at all. Why would they be there? The גמרא will use this to answer the question in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: A place outside the main area of ירושלים
He rebelled (against the ruling of the סנהדרין)
The place is what makes it count

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is about a זקן ממרא, not עגלה ערופה. It is not an obvious answer yet. רב יוסף is only quoting his source here, and the link to our question comes right after.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear:
If he found them at Beit Pagei
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the members of the סנהדרין, and 'he' is the rebellious elder, the זקן ממרא.

phrases.english: and rebelled against them,
one might think his rebellion is a rebellion.
Therefore the verse states:
"And you shall arise and go up to the place,"
which teaches that the place determines it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts an attempt to settle the question asked in Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the entire סנהדרין goes out for measuring according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a זקן ממרא who rebelled against the סנהדרין at בית פגי, based on דברים יז:ח
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא also teaches a rule of its own: the סנהדרין's full authority over a זקן ממרא depends on its sitting in its proper place.

steps.title: How many judges went out to בית פאגי?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף shows that the ברייתא must be talking about the entire סנהדרין going out, not just some of its members.
steps.simpleTranslation: How many judges went out? If you say only some of them, then maybe the judges still inside agree with him, so he is not a rebel at all. So it must be that all of them went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts taking apart the ברייתא about בית פאגי. It asks how many judges were there and concludes that all of them were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only part of the סנהדרין left, the majority might still be sitting in the לשכת הגזית and agree with the זקן. Then he could not be called a rebel. The ברייתא only makes sense if the whole court went out.

phrases.english: How many went out?
phrases.notes: He means: in the ברייתא about בית פאגי, how many of the judges left?

phrases.english: If you say some of them,
perhaps those who are inside
hold like him?
Rather, it is obvious that all of them went out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא quoted by רב יוסף in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How many members of the סנהדרין went out to בית פאגי in the ברייתא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All of them, because otherwise the rebellion would have no meaning.

steps.title: Why did the whole סנהדרין go out?
steps.stepSummary: The whole סנהדרין may not leave for an optional matter, so they must have gone out for a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what purpose did they go out? If you say for an optional matter, are they even allowed to leave? The פסוק says, 'Your navel is like a round goblet, wherein no blended wine is lacking.' So it must have been for a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks why the whole court left its place. It concludes the reason had to be a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in שיר השירים is read as describing the סנהדרין, which must never drop below its required number. So the full court would not all leave for an optional matter. It must have gone out for a required task, which sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a matter connected to a מצוה

phrases.english: For what?
If you say for an optional matter,
are they able to go out?
But isn't it written:
"Your navel is like a round goblet
wherein no blended wine is lacking"!
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 7:3. The סנהדרין sits in a half-circle, like that goblet, and must never drop below its required number.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it was for a מצוה matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 6: now that we know all of them went out, we ask why.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What purpose made the entire סנהדרין leave?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מצוה, since they may not leave for an optional matter.

steps.title: So רבי אליעזר בן יעקב needs the whole סנהדרין
steps.stepSummary: The מצוה must be measuring for the עגלה, which would show that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires the full סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? Isn't it that they went out to measure for the עגלה? And this follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who says we need the whole סנהדרין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף finishes his proof. The full court going out for a מצוה must be the measuring for the עגלה, so רבי אליעזר בן יעקב needs every member there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This would answer the question from step 4. If the whole סנהדרין went out to measure, then the opinion that requires the סנהדרין for measuring must mean all of it, and that opinion is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's. אביי challenges this proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the measuring done for the עגלה ערופה

phrases.english: What is the case?
Isn't it for measuring for the heifer,
and it is the view of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov,
who says: we require the entire Sanhedrin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning from steps 6 and 7 and applies it to the question of step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires the entire סנהדרין for measuring.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the זקן ממרא at בית פאגי, where the full court left for a מצוה.

steps.title: אביי: maybe they went out to enlarge the city
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. The full court may have gone out to add to ירושלים or the עזרות, which needs a court of 71.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: No. It could be a case where they went out to add onto the city and the courtyards. As we learned: they only add onto the city and the courtyards with a court of seventy-one.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף. He says there is a different מצוה that needs the whole court, so the ברייתא proves nothing about measuring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Enlarging ירושלים or the עזרות of the מקדש needs all 71 judges. So the full court could have gone out to בית פאגי for that reason. Then the ברייתא tells us nothing about how many judges measure for the עגלה.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: אביי said to him: No,
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב יוסף, who brought the ברייתא.

phrases.english: such as where they went out
to add onto the city and onto the courtyards,
as we learned:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹסִיפִין עַל הָעִיר וְעַל הָעֲזָרוֹת
phrases.english: They do not add onto the city or onto the courtyards

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: except with a court of seventy-one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לָא, כְּגוֹן שֶׁיָּצְאוּ לְהוֹסִיף עַל הָעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of step 8 by offering another reason the full court went out.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the ברייתא. It does not decide what רבי אליעזר בן יעקב actually holds.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא could be talking about another מצוה that needs 71 judges, so it does not have to be measuring.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא openly mentions the court going out to measure for the עגלה, which supports רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that supports רב יוסף: If the זקן found them at בית פאגי and rebelled against them, for example when they went out to measure for the עגלה or to add onto the city and courtyards, you might think his rebellion counts. So the פסוק says, 'And you shall arise and go up to the place.' This teaches that the place is what gives it force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says outright that the court went out to measure for the עגלה. This backs up רב יוסף against אביי's pushback.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the court may have gone out only to enlarge the city. But this ברייתא lists measuring for the עגלה as one of the reasons the full court leaves. So there is a תנא who holds that all the judges take part in measuring, as רב יוסף said.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא was taught that supports him
a rebellion against the court's ruling
the place is what determines it

steps.whyThisMatters: It settles the question from step 4 in favor of רב יוסף. According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the measuring needs the entire סנהדרין.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav Yosef:
If he found them at Beit Pagei
and rebelled against them,
such as where they went out to measure for the heifer
and to add onto the city and onto the courtyards,
one might think his rebellion counts as a rebellion?
The verse teaches:
"And you shall arise and go up to the place,"
which teaches that the place determines it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overrides אביי's pushback in step 9 by bringing a ברייתא that names measuring for the עגלה.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that measuring for the עגלה involves the entire סנהדרין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing measuring for the עגלה as a reason the full court left for בית פאגי.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the entire סנהדרין goes out to measure for the עגלה ערופה. The ברייתא of בית פאגי supports this.

steps.title: New line of the משנה: valuing produce whose value is unknown
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: three judges value נטע רבעי and מעשר שני whose value is not known.
steps.simpleTranslation: נטע רבעי and מעשר שני whose value is not known are valued by three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the עגלה topic and quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up the ברייתות that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you redeem נטע רבעי and מעשר שני at their known market price. When the price is unclear, a panel of three must set the value.

keyTerms.meaning: fruit from a tree's fourth year, which is redeemed like מעשר שני
the second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money

phrases.english: A fourth-year sapling and second tithe
whose value is not known, by three.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶטַע רְבָעִי וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁאֵין דָּמָיו יְדוּעִין, בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic from the משנה, separate from the עגלה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three people value נטע רבעי and מעשר שני whose value is not known.

steps.title: What counts as מעשר שני with an unknown value
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines it as rotting fruit, wine with a film, or rusted coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: What is מעשר שני whose value is not known? Fruit that began to rot, wine that developed a film, and coins that rusted.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains which kinds of מעשר שני are called 'value not known.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: These items are damaged, so there is no set market price for them. That is why experts are needed to judge how much they are worth.

keyTerms.meaning: that developed a film on top

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Which is second tithe
whose value is not known?
Fruits that have begun to rot,
and wine that has developed a film,
and coins that have rusted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁאֵין דָּמָיו יְדוּעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case mentioned in the משנה in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damaged fruit, wine, or coins of מעשר שני count as having an unknown value.

steps.title: Who may value it: three buyers
steps.stepSummary: The valuing must be done by three people experienced in buying. One of them may even be a גוי or the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: מעשר שני whose value is not known is redeemed by three buyers, but not by three who are not buyers. This holds even if one of them is a גוי, and even if one of them is the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא explains who the 'three' in the משנה must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three do not need to be judges. They need to be people who know the market. Because what matters is knowledge of prices, even a גוי or the owner may be one of the three.
steps.confusionAlert: Here the 'three' are not three judges. They are three people who know prices, so even a גוי or the owner can be one of them.
steps.whatToRemember: מעשר שני whose value is not known is valued by three people who know the market. One of them may even be a גוי or the owner.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: second tithe
whose value is not known
is redeemed by three buyers,
but not by three who are not buyers.
Even if one of them is a גוי,
even if one of them is the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁאֵין דָּמָיו יְדוּעִין, פּוֹדִין אוֹתוֹ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה לָקוֹחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains who the three in the משנה must be.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The redemption must be done by three experienced buyers. A גוי or the owner may be one of them.

steps.title: Can three partners count as three valuers?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether three people who share one purse count as three separate valuers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asks: three people who put their money into one purse, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a new question about the valuers of מעשר שני. If three partners share their money, do they count as three valuers?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said even the owner may be one of the three valuers. So the question is whether partners count as three separate people, or as one 'owner' because their money is mixed together.

keyTerms.meaning: He asks (a real question of law)
They put their money into one purse (full partners)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asks:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה וּמְטִילִין לְתוֹךְ כִּיס אֶחָד, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: Three who put [their money] into one purse, what is [the law]?
phrases.notes: Partners who share all their money: do they count as three people, or as just one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that three experienced people, even the owner, may do the valuing
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether three partners with shared money count as three valuers

steps.title: Proof from a man and his two wives
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a man and his two wives may redeem מעשר שני whose value is not known. This suggests that people who share money count as three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a man and his two wives may redeem מעשר שני whose value is not known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רבי ירמיה's question from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband and wives normally share one household's money. The ברייתא still lets them serve as the three valuers, so partners should count as three.

keyTerms.meaning: A man and his two wives

phrases.english: Come and hear: a man and his two wives
may redeem second tithe
whose value is not known.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question of step 14
steps.raayaObject: That partners sharing money count as three valuers
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: a man and his two wives may redeem מעשר שני

steps.title: Maybe the wives had their own money
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The case may be a couple who kept separate finances, like רב פפא and the daughter of אבא סוראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is like רב פפא and the daughter of אבא סוראה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא may be talking about a special marriage where each spouse had separate money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband and wives kept their money apart, they are not like partners with one purse. So the ברייתא proves nothing about real partners, and רבי ירמיה's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Such as, like the case of

phrases.english: Perhaps [it is] like Rav Pappa
and the daughter of Abba of Sura.
phrases.notes: He means a couple who kept their money separate, so they are not like partners sharing one purse.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא כְּגוֹן רַב פָּפָּא וּבַת אַבָּא סוּרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 15
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The question itself stays unresolved.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be talking about spouses with separate finances, not shared money
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה's question about partners with one purse is left without a proof.

steps.title: Consecrated items need three, but one תנא says ten
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says הקדשות are valued by three. The גמרא notes this does not follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who requires ten people even for a tiny item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Consecrated items are valued by three. Our משנה is not like this תנא, as it is taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, even a small fork of הקדש needs ten people to redeem it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. It points out that a ברייתא records a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (the רבנן) says three judges value הקדש. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says ten, even for something as small as a fork. So the משנה is not following him.

keyTerms.meaning: Items consecrated to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Consecrated items [are valued] by three.
Our Mishnah is not like this Tanna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
even a small fork of consecrated property
needs ten people to redeem it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה requires three for הקדש. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires ten.

steps.title: Where do the רבנן get the number three?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי: ten makes sense based on שמואל's count of 'כהן' in the פרשה, but where do the רבנן get three?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Granted according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, since he holds like שמואל, as שמואל said: ten 'כהנים' are written in the פרשה. But according to the רבנן, from where do they get three?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks for the source of the רבנן's number. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ten has a clear source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל counts the word 'כהן' ten times in the פרשה of הקדש, which gives רבי אליעזר בן יעקב his ten judges. The רבנן's number three has no source yet, so רב פפא asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do they know it?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Granted according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,
since he holds like Shmuel, as Shmuel said:
Ten 'kohanim' are written in the section,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27. Each time the word 'כהן' appears there, one more judge is added.

phrases.english: but according to the Rabbis, from where do they get three?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the רבנן's view quoted in step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for requiring three judges for הקדש

steps.title: Counting three would make land need only four
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the רבנן count 'כהן' three times in the verses about movable הקדש. But then land, where 'כהן' is written four times, should need only four.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that three are written about them, then land, about which four are written, should be enough with four?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible source for three, then immediately attacks it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule is 'count the word כהן in the verses about this item', then land gets four, since 'כהן' appears four times there. This sets up the problem in the next step.

phrases.english: And if you say that three are written about them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the verses about a consecrated animal, where 'כהן' appears three times.

phrases.english: land, about which four are written,
should be enough with four?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to step 18 and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the רבנן count 'כהן' only in the verses about each type of item
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Using the same method, land would need four judges

steps.title: But the משנה says land needs nine and a כהן
steps.stepSummary: Saying land really needs only four does not work, because the משנה says land is valued by nine and a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: indeed so, why did we learn: land is valued by nine and a כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the escape of accepting four for land. The משנה clearly says ten for land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The counting method gives four for land, but the משנה's rule for land is nine plus a כהן. So this method cannot be how the רבנן get three, and the question of step 18 stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Why then did we learn (in the משנה)?

phrases.english: And if you say: indeed so,
why did we learn:
land [is valued by] nine and a kohen?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי אַלְּמָה תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off the possible escape from step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: Accepting that land needs only four
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly requires nine and a כהן for land, so the counting method fails
steps.whatToRemember: The simple counting of 'כהן' cannot explain the רבנן's three. The גמרא still needs another source.

steps.title: A running count of 'כהן' would make הקדשות need six judges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests counting all mentions of 'כהן' in one running total, so that land reaches ten. It rejects this because הקדשות would then reach six and need six judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what will you say? That the count of ten is completed with these verses? Then for הקדשות, where the count reaches six, we should need six judges!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new way to get to the number ten for land: keep one running count of every 'כהן' from the start of the פרשה. Then it shows this idea leads to a wrong result for הקדשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19, the problem was that land has only four mentions of 'כהן', so land should need only four judges. The new idea adds up all the mentions from the start of the פרשה, so by the land verses the total is ten. But by the same method, the running total at the הקדש verses is six, and the משנה says הקדשות need only three.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what [will you say]? This introduces a new suggestion.
Completed, filled up (here: the total count reaches a number)
Items dedicated to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rather, what will you say?
That ten are completed with them?
phrases.notes: He means you count every 'כהן' from the start of the פרשה, so by the land verses the total comes to ten.

phrases.english: Consecrated items, where six are completed with them,
should require six!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new counting method to answer step 20, and shows at once that it fails
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea of counting 'כהן' as one running total through the parsha
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A running total gives ten at the land verses but six at the הקדש verses. Then הקדשות should need six judges, yet the משנה says three.

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with 'קשיא', which means the difficulty about the רבנן's source for three judges is left without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no good answer to where the רבנן get the number three from the verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every counting method tried in steps 19 to 21 failed. 'קשיא' marks this as a real problem that is left standing. It does not mean the רבנן's ruling is thrown out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult. The challenge is left unanswered, but the ruling is not rejected.

steps.whatToRemember: No source in the verses is found for the רבנן's three judges for הקדשות. The גמרא closes this question with 'קשיא'.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' at the end of a discussion is not the same as 'תיובתא'. The question remains open, but the רבנן's view is not refuted.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the line of questioning that רב פפא opened in step 18
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The source in the verses for the רבנן's three judges stays an unresolved difficulty.

steps.title: What does 'valuations of movable property' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה and asks what ערכין of movable property could mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'The valuations, etc.' What does 'valuations of movable property' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new phrase in the משנה and asks what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערכין usually means a vow to give a person's fixed value, as set out in the תורה. That value is set and has nothing to do with objects. So it is unclear how ערכין can apply to movable things.

keyTerms.meaning: Valuations. Usually a vow to give a person's fixed value as set in the תורה.
Etc. The rest of the משנה's wording is understood.

phrases.english: "The valuations, etc."
What are "valuations of movable property"?
phrases.notes: ערכין normally means a person's set value from ויקרא 27:1–8, which doesn't seem to fit objects.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next phrase of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the משנה means by ערכין of movable property

steps.title: Someone said 'the ערך of this utensil is upon me'
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב explains that the case is someone who vowed to give the ערך of a utensil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: it is where a person says, 'The valuation of this utensil is upon me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב גידל answers the question by describing the case: a person used the word ערך about an object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An object has no fixed Torah value, so the person must mean its actual worth. That is why judges are needed to estimate it. This explains how the משנה can speak of ערכין for movable things.

keyTerms.meaning: "The valuation of this utensil is upon me"

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
When one says, "The valuation of this utensil is upon me."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב בְּאוֹמֵר עֵרֶךְ כְּלִי זֶה עָלַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is a person who vowed the ערך of a utensil, so its value must be estimated.

steps.title: Bringing in another teaching of רב גידל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to quote another statement of רב גידל in the name of רב to back up this explanation. The statement itself comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב גידל said that רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote a related ruling of רב גידל that supports his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דְּ' (as) shows that a known teaching is being brought in to explain why his answer works. The content of that teaching comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: As he said. This introduces a supporting statement.

phrases.english: As Rav Giddel said that Rav said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a supporting citation for the answer in step 24
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A further ruling of רב גידל in the name of רב, given on the next amud, supports the explanation of step 24.
